title: A save format, reversed
description:
Work out a simple save format from samples, then write a reader and writer that round-trip.

```
sample A (name "ada", level 3):  58 53 01 03 61 64 61 03 00 D8
sample B (name "bob", level 12): 58 53 01 03 62 6F 62 0C 00 EE
fields: magic "XS", version 1, name length, name, level (u16), checksum
checksum = sum of the bytes before it, & 0xFF
writer output matches both samples exactly
```
hints: Change one thing between samples (only the level) and see which bytes change (lesson 6.02).
Check the checksum guess against every sample before trusting it.
requirements: Compare the samples byte by byte and write down what each byte means.
A reader that checks the magic, version and checksum, and a writer.
Read then write each sample, and check the bytes are identical.
stretch: Make a sample with a long name and check your guess about the length field.
